bib.title: AGIEval: A Human-Centric Benchmark for Evaluating Foundation Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "AGIEval: A Human-Centric Benchmark for Evaluating Foundation Models", Wanjun Zhong, Ruixiang Cui (equal contribution), Yiduo Guo, Yaobo Liang, Shuai Lu, Yanlin Wang, Amin Saied, Weizhu Chen, Nan Duan. Preprint: no venue is printed, only "arXiv:2304.06364v2 [cs.CL] 18 Sep 2023". The only affiliation printed, for all authors, is "Microsoft".
File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/08-eval/sources/zhong-2023-agieval.pdf

COVERAGE: 22 of 22 pages, 83,130 of 83,130 chars, including Appendix A (examples) and Appendix B (contamination, Table 5). References (pp. 17-20) were skimmed. The bar values in Figures 1 and 3 are charts and did not extract.

CLAIMS

- claim: The benchmark is 8,062 objective questions across 20 tasks, in English and Chinese.
  number: 8,062 questions; 20 tasks
  setup: Gaokao has 9 tasks (2,080 items), SAT 2 (426), Chinese lawyer qualification via JEC-QA 2 (2,000), LSAT 3 (1,000, exams from 1991-2016), Chinese civil service via LogiQA en/ch (651 each), GRE/GMAT via AQuA-RAT (254), AMC/AIME via MATH (1,000). Subjective questions were removed. Only Gaokao and SAT were newly collected; the rest are reused public datasets.
  quote: "we construct a benchmark consisting of 8,062 questions for evaluation"
  where: p6, Table 1 p7

- claim: Human baselines are not measured on these items; they are either copied from the source datasets' papers or estimated from scaled exam scores.
  number: average = 50th percentile, top = top 1% (top 10% for the lawyer test, per Fig. 1)
  setup: all tasks. The same pair is reused across sections: LSAT 56/91 for AR, LR and RC; SAT 66/94 for Math and English.
  quote: "for AQuA-RAT (GMAT, GRE), LSAT, SAT, and Gaokao, we estimated the human performances by scaling the scores of the average (50%) and top (1%) test takers against the full scores to 100"
  where: p6

- claim: GPT-4 is below the human average overall, and beats it only on some tasks.
  number: 58.4 (zero-shot CoT) and 61.3 (few-shot CoT) against human 67 average / 91 top
  setup: GPT-4 through the Azure chat API, temperature 0, 5-shot for few-shot. Zero-shot CoT, GPT-4 vs human average: SAT-Math 95.0 vs 66, LSAT-LR 80.6 vs 56, LSAT-RC 85.1 vs 56, MATH 47.7 vs 40, GK-En 92.5 vs 69; but LSAT-AR 34.4 vs 56, JEC-QA-KD 31.9 vs 71, AQuA-RAT 73.2 vs 85, GK-physics 45.5 vs 71.
  quote: "Average 67 91 38.1 42.9 56.4 37.4 43.2 58.4"
  where: Table 2 p10; Table 3 p10

- claim: Few-shot adds little over zero-shot, and CoT helps unevenly.
  number: GPT-4 average 56.4 zero-shot, 59.2 few-shot. CoT lifts SAT-Math from 64.6 to 95.0 and lowers GK-Cn from 53.3 to 44.7.
  setup: as above
  quote: "few-shot learning generally leads to only a limited improvement in performance compared to zero-shot learning"
  where: p11

- claim: The contamination check covers only six Gaokao subjects, comparing the full set with 2022 items that postdate GPT-4's September 2021 cutoff.
  number: MathQA 47% to 29.8% (n=47), math cloze 16.1% to 4% (n=25), chemistry 51.7% to 42.2% (n=64), geography 76.9% to 73% (n=37), biology 75.7% to 77.6% (n=58), physics 39% to 40% (n=5)
  setup: GPT-4 zero-shot
  quote: "barring the Mathematics subjects, the performance experiences a minor drop in the absence of contamination"
  where: pp. 20-22, Table 5

- claim: The error analysis found reasoning the weakest of four dimensions.
  number: 100 wrong answers per task, scored 0/1 on understanding, knowledge, reasoning and calculation
  setup: ChatGPT (not GPT-4), zero-shot CoT, annotated by PhD students and researchers. Named failure types: ignoring premises, confusing sufficient and necessary conditions, counterfactuals, multi-hop chains, fixing a conclusion first, swapping similar concepts, long contexts, variable substitution.
  quote: "sampling 100 errorly answered instances for each task"
  where: pp. 12-16

LIMITS
- Conceded by the authors: human accuracies are "a useful approximation"; "AGIEval may similarly encounter data contamination"; the set is objective questions and text only.
- Not shown (my reading, not stated in the paper):
  - Humans and models are not compared like for like. Human figures are whole-exam scaled scores, which include the removed subjective questions and other exam years; model figures are accuracy on an objective subset.
  - The paper does not say who the test-takers were for MATH, LogiQA or JEC-QA.
  - Contamination is untested for LSAT, SAT and the four reused datasets, all public before the cutoff.
  - Table 5 has no confidence intervals, and the 9.5-point chemistry drop is described as "minor".
  - GPT-4 scores 51.0 zero-shot on SAT-English with the passage removed; the paper does not discuss this.
  - No inter-annotator agreement is reported for the error analysis.
  - JEC-QA "test" items are the first 1,000 training examples.
- Dated: the models are GPT-4, ChatGPT, Text-Davinci-003 and Vicuna-13B, all from 2023.

BUILDS ON: MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2020); CoT (Wei et al., 2022); zero-shot CoT prompt (Zhang et al., 2022b); data from Wang et al. (2022), Zhong et al. (2022), LogiQA (Liu et al., 2021), MATH (Hendrycks et al.), AQuA-RAT (Ling et al., 2017), JEC-QA (Zhong et al., 2020); few-shot MATH examples from Lewkowycz et al. (2022).

CODE: none. The prompt templates are in Fig. 2, p8 ("Let's think step by step", then "Among A to D, the answer is:").

FIGURES: Figure 1, p2. Bars per exam for average human, top human and the three models under zero-shot CoT. It shows at a glance that GPT-4 beats the average on some exams and sits below the top on all of them.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions.
- Chart values in Figs. 1 and 3 could not be read, so no per-dimension error scores are reported.
- The paper is inconsistent on Gaokao-English: 92.5% in the abstract (zero-shot CoT) and 93.8% on p11 (few-shot).
- p6 mislabels JEC-QA as the "Chinese Civil Service Examination".
- p11 cites "Fig. 4" for the Vicuna results, which are in Table 4.
- Appendix B says both "later than 2022" and "released in 2022".
